role.altitude: The fashion designer keeps sketching ideas, judging samples on the model, choosing materials and talking with sales and clients; redrawing technical flats, retyping tech packs, recolouring by hand and hunting for material data shrink.
skills_to_grow: Keeping flat, colour and material libraries tidy
role.ambitious_version: A designer whose tech packs build themselves from the flat and the material library, leaving more time at the fitting table.

tasks.short: Sketch rough drawings of apparel and accessories, draw the detailed technical drawing, prepare colourways, write specifications such as color schemes, construction, material types and accessory requirements, and check the tech pack.

steps.what: Designer sketches rough drawings of apparel and accessories
Designer draws the detailed technical drawing of the garment
Designer prepares colourway variants of the flat
Designer writes specifications: color schemes, construction, material types and accessory requirements
Designer checks the final tech pack

tasks.design: Rough sketching stays by hand. Technical flats start from the designer's library of base flats in drawing software instead of being drawn from scratch, and colourways are made by swapping the season's palette onto the flat. The tech pack is built in a product lifecycle system that takes the flat and picks colours, materials and trims from libraries, instead of retyping them into a spreadsheet. The designer checks the final tech pack.
tasks.previous_blocker: Flats were redrawn and tech packs retyped for each style.
tasks.enabler_now: Flat libraries and product lifecycle systems with material and trim libraries.
tasks.still_hard: New silhouettes with no base flat.
tasks.altitude: Less redrawing and retyping; design stays.

evidence.claim: Product lifecycle systems keep material and trim libraries that fill tech packs.

assumptions: Boundary: drawings and specifications for a style; patterns and samples are outside.
Input contract for s4: materials and trims kept in the product lifecycle system by the material developer; about 80% of styles use library items; s4 is priced at that share.
Sketching and checking keep their full time.
unknowns: Share of styles that start from a base flat.
research_questions: Do tech pack errors in first samples fall?

incremental.description: Designer keeps base flats and the season palette current.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: mostly new silhouettes with no base flat and new materials (s2 95, s4 80) (10.2); high: carry-over styles at about 80% library coverage (21.5).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Examine sample garments on and off models, decide modifications to achieve desired effects, record fit comments and update the design and specifications for the next sample.

steps.what: Designer examines sample garments on and off models
Designer decides modifications to the designs to achieve the desired effects
Designer records fit comments with photos and measurements
Designer updates the design and specifications for the next sample
Designer checks the revised tech pack before release: every decided change is in it, measurements and materials are right
Designer releases the checked revision to the sample room

tasks.design: Examining samples and deciding changes stay at the fitting table. Fit comments go into the sample record on a tablet, with photos and a measurement table already filled with the specified values, so the designer types only actual measurements and comments; writing them keeps most of its time. Changes are made in the tech pack with revisions tracked, and the designer checks the revision and releases it once to the sample room instead of mailing a new spreadsheet version.

approvals.approved_version: The revised tech pack exactly as checked by the designer in s4b, released once to the sample room for the next sample; any change needs a new check.

tasks.previous_blocker: Fit comments were written on paper and retyped into mails and spreadsheets.
tasks.enabler_now: Sample records on tablets linked to the tech pack.
tasks.still_hard: Effects that depend on how fabric moves.
tasks.human_edge: Seeing that a garment does not feel right on the body.

reach.learn: Whether fewer sample rounds are needed.

evidence.claim: Sample records with photos and measurement tables are a standard product lifecycle function.

assumptions: Boundary: judging samples and passing changes on; making samples is outside.
Input contract for s3: specified measurements taken from the tech pack.

Examining and deciding keep their full time. s3 keeps 80: specified values are filled in, but actual measurements and comments are first records. s4 keeps 70 because a new spreadsheet version is no longer built and mailed.
unknowns: Number of sample rounds per style.
research_questions: Do sample rounds per style fall?

incremental.description: Designer photographs samples consistently for the record.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: few comments per fitting, so pre-filled values save little (s3 90, s4 85) (3.4); high: detailed fit rounds with many measurements (7.4).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Prepare the line presentation, confer with sales and management executives or clients to discuss design ideas, note decisions per style and answer follow-up questions.

steps.what: Designer prepares the presentation boards with sketches, colourways and prices
Designer confers with sales and management executives or clients to discuss design ideas
Designer notes the decision for each style: kept, changed or dropped
Designer answers follow-up questions from sales and clients

tasks.design: Line boards are built from the styles in the product lifecycle system with flats, colourways and target prices placed by a board template, instead of assembled slide by slide. In the meeting, decisions are ticked per style on the same line list. Talking with sales, management and clients stays fully personal.
tasks.previous_blocker: Boards were assembled by hand and decisions written up afterwards.
tasks.enabler_now: Line board templates fed from the product lifecycle system.
tasks.human_edge: Telling the story behind a collection.

evidence.claim: Templates with locked areas can be filled with variants from a spreadsheet.

assumptions: Boundary: discussing design ideas with sales, management and clients; selling is outside.
Input contract for s1: styles, flats and target prices kept in the product lifecycle system by the design team.
Meetings and follow-up keep their full time. s3 keeps 80: ticking decisions on the line list saves retyping style names, but recording each decision is a first record.
unknowns: Number of line reviews per season.
research_questions: Are decisions clearer to the sample room?

incremental.description: Designer keeps the board template current.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: few, informal meetings with few boards (s1 85) (5.4); high: large line reviews with many styles (11.7).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Look up material data from suppliers, handle and test swatches, select materials and production techniques for the products, and record the choices in the tech pack.

steps.what: Designer looks up material data: composition, weight, price, minimums and lead time
Designer selects materials and production techniques for the products
Designer records the chosen materials and techniques in the tech pack

tasks.design: A material library in the product lifecycle system holds each approved material with composition, weight, price, minimums, lead time and test results, filterable by need, instead of searching supplier mails and price lists. Handling swatches and choosing stay with the designer. The chosen material is picked from the library into the tech pack.
tasks.previous_blocker: Material data sat in supplier mails and price lists.
tasks.enabler_now: Material libraries in product lifecycle systems.
tasks.still_hard: New materials no supplier has tested yet.

reach.learn: Which materials designers search for and do not find.

evidence.claim: Catalogue tools build priced article lists that replace manual lookups.

assumptions: Boundary: choosing materials and techniques; buying them is sourcing's.
Input contract for s1: the material developer keeps approved materials and supplier data in the library, about 70% of materials used; s1 is priced at that share.
Handling and choosing keep their full time.
unknowns: Share of new materials per season.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: many new materials outside the library (s1 85, s4 80) (7.2); high: mostly approved materials at about 70% coverage (19.2).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional
